topPRs.title: feat(kona): integrate kona-sp1 into the monorepo
topPRs.author: wwared
topPRs.body:
Closes #18489 and closes #18457.

## Summary

Adds the experimental **kona-sp1** integration — zkVM-based fault proofs for OP Stack state transitions, built on [SP1](https://github.com/succinctlabs/sp1) — under `rust/kona/sp1/`.

> ⚠️ **Experimental.** Establishes the crate structure and host/guest baseline. Not wired into production proving; not for production use.

## Provenance

Derived from [OP-Succinct](https://github.com/succinctlabs/op-succinct) via the standalone op-rs/kona prototype at https://github.com/op-rs/kona/pull/3051 (SP1 v5.2.2). That PR was cut from an older op-succinct (≈ v3.3.5); this PR re-aligns the host/client crates to current op-succinct, then adapts everything to the monorepo and SP1 v6.2.4.

## Scope

Ports only the **proving core**: op-succinct's `utils/{client,host,build,ethereum}` and the `range`/`aggregation` guest programs. Excludes op-succinct's `validity`, `fault-proof`, `contracts`, `bindings`, `scripts`, `signer`, and `proof` subsystems, and the host modules `block_range`, `l1_selection`, `proof_cache`, `rpc_types`, `witness_cache`. Benchmarking tooling lands separately.

## Changes vs https://github.com/op-rs/kona/pull/3051

Source is structurally inherited (same `kona-sp1-*` crates and layout). On top of it:

- **SP1 v5.2.2 (`inphi/sp1` fork) → v6.2.4 (official crates.io)**; drives the EVM/precompile API updates and ELF changes below.
- **Re-aligned host/client crates to current op-succinct** (the op-rs PR predated these): the GHSA-5jh4-3p33-85xc target-downgrade postcondition, `OpPrecompiles::new_with_spec` precompile construction, SafeDB JSON-RPC error classification, rollup-config caching/validation, KZG `Ok(false)` rejection, the network-prover builder, and panic-elimination.
- **Collapsed the range ELF variants** (`range-elf-bump` + `range-elf-embedded`) into a single `range-elf` (embedded-allocator feature removed in SP1 v6.2.4).
- **Isolated guest crypto patches** into a nested workspace; gitignored generated ELFs.
- Monorepo wiring: workspace members/deps, `deny.toml`, CI protobuf install, `just build-sp1`.

## Changes vs upstream op-succinct

At the **logic level the host/client crates track current op-succinct** (per the re-alignment above). The remaining differences:

**Structure / layout:**
- Crates renamed `op-succinct-*` → `kona-sp1-*`; `utils/` → `crates/`, Kona module layout.
- **Ethereum DA only** — Celestia, EigenDA, and AltDA range programs and their `utils/{celestia,eigenda,altda}` crates are not ported.
- `range/ethereum` + `range/utils` merged into one `range` crate.
- Added Kona-layer crates with no upstream equivalent: `crates/elfs`, `crates/proof`.

**Toolchain:**
- **SP1 v6.2.4** vs op-succinct's **v6.1.0** — pulls in a newer revm/op-revm/alloy-op-evm precompile API (`PrecompileHalt` vs `PrecompileError`, `OpTx`/`OpEvmContext` types, the gas-`reservoir` arg, fluent `Context::mainnet()…build` builder, `report.gas()`).
- A single `range-elf` (no bump/embedded variants).

**Monorepo integration:**
- Guest crypto patches **isolated in a nested `programs/Cargo.toml` workspace** (own `Cargo.lock` + `[patch.crates-io]` for sha2/sha3/crypto-bigint/k256/p256/substrate-bn), so they don't touch the monorepo `rust/` graph (upstream keeps them at its repo root).
- Generated ELFs **gitignored**; `crates/elfs/build.rs` writes empty placeholders when absent, and real ELFs build on demand via `just build-elfs`.
- Host crates wired into the monorepo `rust/` workspace.

**Monorepo-API adaptations** (newer kona/alloy than op-succinct ships):
- `is_interop_active(block_info.timestamp)` (op-succinct passes `number`).
- Blob lookups take `&[B256]` (not `&[IndexedBlobHash]`); extra `None` arg on `OraclePipeline::new`.
- `PostExecEvmFactoryHooks`/`PostExecEvmFactoryAdapter` from the monorepo's `alloy-op-evm`.
- Host-args wiring (`l2_chain_id` populated, `DataFormat::Directory`).

**Port-specific behavior:**
- A **zero-step / trace-extension short-circuit** in the witness executor: when the claimed L2 block equals the agreed safe head there is nothing to derive, so it asserts `claimed_output_root == agreed_output_root` and returns early. Lifted verbatim from kona's native client (`rust/kona/bin/client/src/single.rs`) so the SP1 client handles the same dispute-game edge case; op-succinct only guards `claimed < safe_head`.

**Unchanged:** the guest commitment scheme matches op-succinct (range commits `BootInfoStruct` via `sp1_zkvm::io::commit`; aggregation digests via `bincode::serialize`).

## File mapping (op-succinct → this PR)

| op-succinct | this PR (`rust/kona/sp1/`) |
|---|---|
| `utils/client` (`op-succinct-client-utils`) | `crates/client` (`kona-sp1-client-utils`) |
| `utils/host` (`op-succinct-host-utils`) | `crates/host` (`kona-sp1-host-utils`) |
| `utils/build` (`op-succinct-build-utils`) | `crates/build` (`kona-sp1-build-utils`) |
| `utils/ethereum/client` | `crates/ethereum/client` (`kona-sp1-ethereum-client-utils`) |
| `utils/ethereum/host` | `crates/ethereum/host` (`kona-sp1-ethereum-host-utils`) |
| `programs/range/ethereum` + `programs/range/utils` | `programs/range` (merged) |
| `programs/aggregation` | `programs/aggregation` |
| — (no upstream equivalent) | `crates/elfs`, `crates/proof` |

`crates/client/src/{boot,client,types,oracle/*,precompiles/*,witness/*}` and `crates/host/src/{constants,contract,fetcher,host,logger,metrics,network,proof,stats,witness_generation/*}` map 1:1 to op-succinct's `utils/client/src` and `utils/host/src`.

## Known gaps / follow-ups

- Only the **guest programs** (range, aggregation) are included — no host-side programs; the host crates are libraries only.
- Monorepo CI does not yet install the SP1 toolchain or run the Dockerized ELF build, Codecov wiring, or no-std checks for the SP1 crates (#18326).
- We'll likely want to **rename the crates** once this is made more independent from SP1 and supports different zkVMs.
- Benchmarking harness lands separately.
- It's possible the roundtrip serialization of proof/public values between the range proof and agg proof do not match exactly due to `bincode` weirdness. This can be fixed in a follow-up PR if needed (requires generating two real, full range proofs and aggregating them in one agg proof); this PR chose to minimize changes from upstream op-succinct instead.

topPRs.title: feat(op-supernode): HTTP-backed remote interop nodes
topPRs.author: opsuperchain
topPRs.body:
## What

Adds a **remote node** to `op-supernode`: a participant in the interop set that the supernode does **not** drive. Instead of running a consensus client for the chain, the supernode **polls a remote HTTP endpoint** for that chain's **finalized** initiating messages and seals them into the chain's `LogsDB`. The chains the supernode actually drives can then reference those messages as **executing messages**, exactly as they reference messages originating from driven chains.

The **wire protocol is the plugin boundary** — point a remote node at any server, in any language, that responds correctly:

```
GET {baseURL}/finalized?after={N}
200 application/json:
  { "blockTime": 2,
    "block": { "number": N+1, "hash": "0x..", "parentHash": "0x..",
               "timestamp": 1002, "messages": [ {"logIndex":0,"logHash":"0x.."} ] } }
  // "block": null  ⇒ nothing finalized after N yet
```

Only a real HTTP **client** ships in the binary — there is no mock in production.

## Design

- **`op-supernode/supernode/remote`** (production):
  - `Adapter` — the internal seam the ingester polls.
  - `FinalizedBlock` / `InitiatingMessage` — **normalized initiating messages** grouped into a finalized block; these are also the JSON wire types.
  - `HTTPAdapter` — the production adapter: configured with a URL, polls the protocol above, caches the reported `blockTime`.
- **`interop.remoteNode` + `Interop.AddRemoteNode`** (production) — the ingester: polls an `Adapter` and seals finalized blocks into the per-chain `LogsDB`, mirroring the driven-chain `processBlockLogs` path. **Finalized-only ⇒ no reorg/rewind handling.** Ingesters run as background goroutines started in `Start`.
- **`verifyExecutingMessage`** resolves the *initiating* chain's block time from either a driven chain or a registered remote node (the single behavioral edit to the validation path). Remote nodes only ever appear on the initiating/source side.
- **Config:** `--interop.remote-nodes <chainID>=<url>` (repeatable / comma-separated). The supernode builds an `HTTPAdapter` per entry and registers it.
- **`remote/remotetest`** (test-only) — a deterministic `http.Handler` implementing the protocol. Tests wrap it in `httptest.Server` and point a real `HTTPAdapter` at it, so the production HTTP path is exercised end-to-end. The Go linker keeps it out of release builds.

### Why the served messages are referenceable

`raftwallogdb.DB.Contains` recomputes the message checksum from the **stored log hash** + the DB's chain ID + the sealed block's timestamp. So whatever a remote node serves is referenceable by an executing message that carries the derived checksum — the supernode trusts the (finalized) remote node for its own chain's content.

## Tests

- `remote`: `HTTPAdapter` happy path against the test server (contiguous, linked blocks; `blockTime` cached; `block:null` ⇒ not-yet-finalized), plus non-200 and null-block handling.
- `interop`:
  - `TestRemoteNodeIngestAndContains` — server → `HTTPAdapter` → ingester → `LogsDB.Contains` round-trip (positive) + wrong-checksum rejection (negative), against a real `raftwallogdb`.
  - `TestAddRemoteNode` — registration, duplicate/driven-chain guards.
  - `TestVerifyExecutingMessageReferencesRemoteNode` — a driven chain references a remote node's message (served over HTTP) through the real `verifyExecutingMessage` path (positive + negative).
  - **`TestEngineVerifiesExecutingMessageFromRemoteNode` (engine-level e2e)** — a driven chain emits a **real `CrossL2Inbox` executing-message log** referencing a remote-node-served initiating message; the log is sealed through the production `processBlockLogs` path (real `DecodeExecutingMessageLog`) and validated by the real `verifyInteropMessages` engine. Asserts the block is **accepted** when the reference is valid (and that the block actually carries one decoded executing message, so acceptance isn't vacuous), and **flagged invalid** when the reference is tampered.

`go build ./op-supernode/...`, `go vet`, and `gofmt` are clean; adjacent `config`/`flags`/`supernode` package tests pass.

## Notes / follow-ups

- No real chains/binaries yet: the engine-level e2e drives the real verification engine (`processBlockLogs` → `verifyInteropMessages`) with mock chains. A full devstack e2e (real op-node/op-geth driven L2 + in-process supernode + `remotetest` server, with a real tx emitting the executing message) is a natural follow-up; the supernode already runs in-process in op-e2e / op-devstack.
- The protocol is intentionally minimal (single polling endpoint). Auth, batching (multiple blocks per response), and a metadata/handshake endpoint are natural extensions.

topPRs.title: feat: Super ZK Dispute Game
topPRs.author: 0xarktos
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Migrates `ZKDisputeGame` from single-chain output roots to super-root semantics in place, mirroring `SuperFaultDisputeGame`. Reuses the existing `ZK_DISPUTE_GAME` slot; all callers keep routing through the same addresses.

## Changes

### Contracts — `src/dispute/zk/ZKDisputeGame.sol`

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| `extraData` & CWIA | New variable-length layout: 4 B `parentIndex` ‖ 1 B version ‖ 8 B timestamp ‖ n × 64 B `(chainId, root)` pairs. Hardcoded `0x12E` calldata check replaced with `_verifyInitCallDataLength`; impl-arg getters use dynamic offsets. New internal helpers: `_preExtraDataByteCount`, `_extraDataByteCount`, `gameImplArgsByteCount`, plus public `superRootProof()` returning the canonical SuperRootProof bytes. |
| `rootClaim` | Now `keccak256(SuperRootProof)`, bound at init via `Hashing.hashSuperRootProof(...) == rootClaim`. |
| `l2SequenceNumber` | Semantically u64 timestamp (was u256 block number); read via `_getArgUint64(0x5D)`. `startingBlockNumber()` → `startingSequenceNumber()`. |
| `l2ChainId` | Invariant flipped: `!= 0` → revert `NoChainIdNeeded`. Getter made internal (`_l2ChainId()`); new `error NoChainIdNeeded()` mirrors SFDG. |
| `rootClaimByChainId` | Decodes SuperRootProof, scans pairs, reverts `UnknownChainId` on miss. |
| `prove()` | Drops `l2ChainId` from public values (5 fields instead of 6). |
| Misc | Version `1.2.0` → `2.0.0`. `absolutePrestate` NatSpec flagged as multi-chain super-root vkey. New imports: `Types`, `Encoding`, `Hashing`, `BadExtraData`. |

### Interfaces — `interfaces/dispute/zk/IZKDisputeGame.sol`

| Change | Notes |
|---|---|
| Added `error NoChainIdNeeded()` | Mirrors contract-local declaration |
| Added `superRootProof()` | New view returning the canonical SuperRootProof bytes |
| Renamed `startingBlockNumber()` → `startingSequenceNumber()` | Reflects timestamp semantics |
| Removed `l2ChainId()` | Getter is now internal on the contract |

### Tests

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `test/dispute/DisputeGameFactory.t.sol` | Shared ZK helpers updated: `setupZKDisputeGame` packs `l2ChainId = 0`; new `_makeZKExtraDataAndClaim` overloads; `_zkCreateParams` builds valid SuperRootProof bindings; assertions updated for the new 77-byte minimum extraData. |
| `test/dispute/zk/ZKDisputeGame.t.sol` | `setUp()` + 22 game-creation sites refactored through new `_createZKGame` / `_createZKGameOfType` helpers. New cases: hash-binding mismatch, multi-chain lookup, helper coverage, lower-bound timestamp fuzz (replaces the obsolete uint64-overflow fuzz). |
| `test/dispute/zk/ZKDisputeGameIntegration.t.sol` | `_createGame` rewired to derive `rootClaim` from the output-root label; all three lifecycle scenarios updated. |

## Test Plan

```bash
DEV_FEATURE__ZK_DISPUTE_GAME=true forge test --match-path "test/dispute/zk/*.t.sol"
```
